To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the diurnal hemodynamic profile is altered in ethanol-fed hypertensives; 2) the altered diurnal profile is associated with a shift in the autonomic control of the diurnal profile in ethanol-fed hypertenseives; 3) this autonomic shift is characterized by a loss of diurnal modulation of cardiac sympathetic and parasympathetic tone; and 4) this autonomic modulation is associated with a loss of the normal diurnal modulation in cardiac baroreflex
